data.content_ref: inline:The target claims to 'bypass induction by shifting the framework from justification to selection,' but this is self-undermining. The mechanism states we prefer the best-corroborated theory because 'it is the only one currently known to be adapted to the problem environment.' Yet 'currently known to be adapted' is a description of past performance (it survived tests up to now). If this description carries no implication about the future, then it cannot ground a preference (a normative, forward-looking directive about which theory to adopt going forward). If it DOES carry an implication about future performance — that a theory adapted to past tests will remain adapted — that is precisely induction, the very thing the target claims to bypass. The target's own countercondition flags this ('If biological fitness implies future survival via induction') but never resolves it; the mechanism simply asserts the bypass without discharging the obligation. The analogy thus either collapses into a vacuous report of present status (no preference follows) or smuggles in the induction it purports to avoid.
